original_question: Find the asymptotic value of D3^o(n), the minimum number of distinct distances determined by n points constrained to lie on a sphere in R^3.
target_in_paper: Section 4, Problem 11 in the current arXiv rendering (corresponding to Problem 17 in the June 7, 2014 PDF draft where the notation is displayed explicitly): determine the asymptotic value of D_3^o(n), where D_d^o(n) is the minimum number of distinct distances determined by n points on a hypersphere in R^d. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1406.1949))
correct_elements: Your draft already identifies the correct open problem, the correct ambient dimension, and the correct quantity of interest: it is exactly the sphere-restricted distinct-distances problem in R^3 singled out in Section 4. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1406.1949))
missing_details: State D_3^o(n) formally as a minimum over all n-point sets P that lie on a common sphere S⊂R^3, rather than only describing it informally in words. ([adamsheffer.wordpress.com](https://adamsheffer.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/distprobs3.pdf))

Define the counting function D(P): it is the number of distinct Euclidean distances determined by pairs of distinct points of P. ([adamsheffer.wordpress.com](https://adamsheffer.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/distprobs3.pdf))

Clarify that the distances are ambient Euclidean chord distances in R^3, not geodesic distances measured along the sphere. This is implicit from the paper’s distinct-distances notation. ([adamsheffer.wordpress.com](https://adamsheffer.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/distprobs3.pdf))

Specify that the sphere is any common 2-sphere in R^3 (the paper says a hypersphere in R^d), not a fixed named sphere unless you choose to normalize one. ([adamsheffer.wordpress.com](https://adamsheffer.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/distprobs3.pdf))
Make explicit that 'asymptotic value' means the order of growth as n→∞. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1406.1949))

If you want the question to reflect the nearby context exactly, mention the bounds recorded immediately before the problem: Ω(n/log n) ≤ D_3^o(n) ≤ O(n). ([adamsheffer.wordpress.com](https://adamsheffer.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/distprobs3.pdf))
refined_question: Let D(P) denote the number of distinct Euclidean distances determined by pairs of distinct points of a finite set P⊂R^3. Define D_3^o(n)=min{D(P): |P|=n and P is contained in a common 2-sphere in R^3}. Determine the asymptotic order of growth of D_3^o(n) as n→∞.
justification: The draft is targeting the sphere-restricted higher-dimensional open problem in Section 4, not the general higher-dimensional problem D_3(n) and not the broader d≥4 hypersphere problem. The paper first defines D_d^o(n) for n points on a hypersphere in R^d, then immediately specializes to d=3 with the standalone prompt 'Find the asymptotic value of D_3^o(n).' The adjacent sentences give the intended scope and current status by recording the bounds Ω(n/log n) and O(n). ([adamsheffer.wordpress.com](https://adamsheffer.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/distprobs3.pdf))
